# quantfit

> Quantize an LLM and check it still refuses what it should. A GPU-aware quantization CLI whose distinguishing feature is a **paired** baseline-vs-quantized refusal diff with at-risk denominators and Wilson 95% intervals — it compares a model against its own quantization rather than scoring it in the absolute.

Why paired: published work finds strongly-aligned models robust to quantization and weakly-aligned ones not, so an absolute safety score cannot separate "this model was never well aligned" from "quantization broke it". A diff can.

Every command accepts `--json` and prints exactly one document on stdout. Exit codes are the CI contract: **0** clean, **2** operational error, **3** verdict failed, **4** nothing was measured, **5** the gate cannot resolve the threshold you declared. 4 and 5 are not passes.

To see real output in about a second, with no model, no network and no weights:
`quantfit verify-safety --demo`

## Commands

- [check](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit check --model <hf-id>` — will this model fit your GPU? Exit 3 means it will not.
- [list](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit list` — the supported method × scheme matrix.
- [plan](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit plan --model <hf-id>` — the config quantfit would pick for this machine, and why. Reads the local device only; never reaches the Hub.
- [probe](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit probe --model <hf-id> --bits 4 8` — per-bit-width sensitivity (RTN-KL). An upper bound on degradation, not a verdict.
- [quantize](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit quantize --model <hf-id> --method awq --out ./out` — quantize via llm-compressor or llama.cpp.
- [verify](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit verify --model ./out` — smoke-load the artifact and generate.
- [verify-safety](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit verify-safety --baseline <hf-id> --quant ./out` — the paired refusal diff. This is the command the tool exists for.
- **CI**: add `--junit drift.xml` to any verdict command and the result renders as a test in GitHub Actions, GitLab, Jenkins, Buildkite or CircleCI. One case per axis; an axis with zero at-risk pairs is `skipped`, never `passed`.
- [screen](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit screen --targets targets.json --out ./screen` — run the diff over a manifest and aggregate per-stratum, per-axis prevalence bounds.
- [gate](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/docs/ci-integration.md): `quantfit gate --baseline <hf-id> --quant ./out --tier smoke` — the pre-release check, which refuses a threshold finer than the run could resolve rather than passing it.
- [emit](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit emit model-card --report report.json` — render a model-card fragment from a drift report.
- [calibrate](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/docs/judge-calibration-v0.md): `quantfit calibrate sheet --capture c.capture.jsonl --sheet s.labels.csv --key k.labelkey.json` then `quantfit calibrate ingest --sheet s.labels.csv --key k.labelkey.json --out cal.json` — blinded judge-error measurement.
- [reproduce](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/docs/cross-hardware-tolerance-v0.md): `quantfit reproduce --reference ref.json --candidate cand.json` — does this report reproduce that one, under the cross-hardware tolerance?
- [audit](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/README.md): `quantfit audit` — docs=code parity for this repository itself.

## What a result means

- [The QSR v0 spec](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/spec/qsr-v0.md): the normative protocol — at-risk denominators, the two axes, the verdict strings, the exit-code contract, and what a no-detection result does and does not say.
- [CI integration](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/docs/ci-integration.md): wiring the gate into a release pipeline, and the reference composite action.
- [Cross-hardware tolerance](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/docs/cross-hardware-tolerance-v0.md): when one run counts as reproducing another.
- [Validation matrix](https://github.com/Sahil170595/quantfit/blob/main/docs/validation-matrix.md): what has actually been run, on what hardware, with what evidence. Read this before quoting any number as validated.

## Honest limits

- A no-detection result **bounds** the drift; it does not certify safety. At the shipped probe set's dangerous-axis size that bound is wide.
- The judge is uncalibrated until `calibrate` has been run, so the printed MDE is a perfect-judge floor — a lower bound on the true resolution, never the resolution.
- Only weight quantization is measured. KV-cache quantization, where recent work locates alignment collapse, is not an axis this tool can see.
- Decoding is greedy and the probe set is one curated corpus. Published guidance argues for multi-sample stability across several benchmarks; the trade is determinism and a defensible denominator, and it is stated rather than hidden.
- Every published GPU number in this project comes from one laptop. See the validation matrix.
